## Change

**`src/context.ts:414-437`** — the `res` setter no longer discards the incoming response's cookies. Before merging the old response headers, it now captures both cookie sets, clears the field, and re-appends previous cookies first, then the new response's cookies:

```ts
const cookies = this.#res.headers.getSetCookie()
const newCookies = _res.headers.getSetCookie()
if (cookies.length || newCookies.length) {
  _res.headers.delete('set-cookie')
  for (const cookie of cookies) _res.headers.append('set-cookie', cookie)
  for (const cookie of newCookies) _res.headers.append('set-cookie', cookie)
}
```

The old per-header branch was hoisted out of the `entries()` loop because in this runtime `Headers.entries()` yields `set-cookie` once per cookie — running the merge per entry duplicated cookies (observed as 5 instead of 3). The loop now skips `set-cookie` and keeps the rest of the merge semantics (content-type skip, other headers `set`, immutable-response cloning, `finalized = true`) intact.
